To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
all equations for estimating glomerular filtration in children after renal or cardiac transplantation or post-therapy are inaccurate.
none of the eight eGFR estimation equations performed well in our cohort, but the CKiD III, the Hoste, and the Grubb equations performed slightly better than the Schwartz equation.

the eGFR equations evaluated in this study were not accurate in children after renal or cardiac transplantation or post-therapy treatment, and that they should therefore not be used for staging of the CKD in this population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of which eGFR equation is best suited for use in pediatric renal or transplant patients.
the impact of eGFR equations on clinical management and CKD staging of children after renal transplantation, heart transplantation or post chemotherapy.
the impact of the eGFR equations used in the clinical management of pediatric patients with CKD after renal transplantation or chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all eight eGGR equations are unsuitable for clinical management of children with renal or heart transplantation.
the Schwartz equation is a good alternative for the inulin clearance in the pediatric population.
none of the eGFR equations evaluated in this study can be recommended for clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Schwartz equation is a good choice for a bedside estimation of renal function in children.
none of the evaluated eGFR equations are accurate enough for clinical use in children with renal or heart transplants.
none of the equations evaluated is suitable for the routine clinical management of children who have received a kidney or heart transplant or have been treated with chemotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of eGFR equation may influence the staging of CKD and thus the clinical management of the patients, especially in children with decreased GFR.

none of the evaluated eGFR equations is suitable to replace the inulin clearance in the assessment of renal function after renal or heart transplantations or post-chemotherapeutic treatment in children.
the use of any eGFR equation in children after renal or cardiac transplantation may result in a significant misdiagnosis of their CKD stage and thus lead to inappropriate clinical management.
